rules.source: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) as amended by CPRA (Prop. 24); regulations by California Privacy Protection Agency — https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/ccpa
rules.retrieved_snippet: California AG: rights include to know, delete, opt out of sale or sharing, correct, and limit use of sensitive personal information; applies to for-profit businesses meeting revenue (over $25 million) or data-volume thresholds; private suits limited to data breaches.

rules.source: SB 53, Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act (Ch. 138, Stats. 2025), signed Sept. 29, 2025 — https://www.gov.ca.gov/2025/09/29/governor-newsom-signs-sb-53-advancing-californias-world-leading-artificial-intelligence-industry/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Governor's release/search summary: large frontier AI developers must publish a frontier AI framework, critical safety incidents are reported to the Office of Emergency Services, whistleblowers are protected, and the Attorney General enforces civil penalties.

rules.source: AB 2013, Generative artificial intelligence: training data transparency (signed Sept. 28, 2024) — https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240AB2013
rules.retrieved_snippet: Search summary of bill text: AI developers must post on their websites a high-level summary of datasets used to develop generative AI systems on or before January 1, 2026.

Search summary: covered providers must offer free AI-detection tools, visible markings on AI-generated content and latent provenance disclosures where technically feasible, from January 1, 2026; later operative-date changes not verified.
